subject: ela
intro: Each question gives you a short written passage and a non-text format, such as a table, chart, timeline, map, or diagram described in words. Read both sources, then choose the answer that correctly combines them. Pick the single best answer.

items.prompt:
Passage: The town of Maple Creek planted a public garden in 2018. Every spring, volunteers add new flower beds. The garden has grown larger every year since it opened.

Table 1: Number of flower beds at Maple Creek Garden
Year 2018: 4 beds
Year 2019: 6 beds
Year 2020: 9 beds

Which row of the table best supports the sentence that the garden has grown larger every year?
A) Year 2018: 4 beds, because that is when the garden opened
B) The fact that 2018 has 4, 2019 has 6, and 2020 has 9, because the number rises each year
C) Year 2020: 9 beds, because 9 is the largest number
D) The table does not support the sentence at all
items.answer: B) The fact that 2018 has 4, 2019 has 6, and 2020 has 9, because the number rises each year

steps: The sentence claims the garden grew larger every year, which is a trend over time, not a single value.
To support a trend, you must show the number rising each year: 4, then 6, then 9. Choice B shows that climb, so it is correct.
A only names the starting point and shows growth for one year, not every year.
C reports the largest single number straight from the table without connecting it to the idea of growth over time.
D is wrong because the rising numbers clearly back up the claim.
solution.answer: B) The fact that 2018 has 4, 2019 has 6, and 2020 has 9, because the number rises each year

items.prompt:
Passage: The school library is busiest right after lunch. Many students come in during the early afternoon to study. The crowd thins out by the end of the school day.

Table 1: Visitors to the school library by hour
9 a.m.: 12 visitors
12 p.m.: 20 visitors
1 p.m.: 35 visitors
3 p.m.: 8 visitors

Which entry in the table best confirms that the library is busiest right after lunch?
A) 9 a.m.: 12 visitors
B) 12 p.m.: 20 visitors
C) 1 p.m.: 35 visitors
D) 3 p.m.: 8 visitors

steps: Lunch happens around noon, so 'right after lunch' points to the 1 p.m. hour.
The 1 p.m. row shows 35 visitors, the highest count in the table, which confirms the busiest time. Choice C is correct.
A (9 a.m.) is the morning, before lunch.
B (12 p.m.) is during lunch, not after it, and shows fewer visitors than 1 p.m.
D (3 p.m.) is the end of the day when the crowd has thinned, the opposite of busiest.

items.prompt:
Passage: A diagram in the article shows how a paper airplane flies. The passage explains that air pushing up on the wings keeps the plane in the air. The article calls this upward push 'lift.'

Diagram 1: Forces on a paper airplane
An arrow labeled 'lift' points up from the wings.
An arrow labeled 'weight' points down from the body.
An arrow labeled 'thrust' points forward from the nose.

How does the diagram help you understand the sentence about lift?
A) It shows that lift is an upward arrow on the wings, matching the text's idea of an upward push
B) It shows that the plane is made of paper
C) It just decorates the article and adds no information
D) It proves the plane cannot fly
items.answer: A) It shows that lift is an upward arrow on the wings, matching the text's idea of an upward push

steps: The text says lift is an upward push on the wings.
The diagram labels an arrow 'lift' pointing up from the wings, which pictures exactly what the words describe. Choice A correctly links the two sources.
B reports a detail (paper) that does not connect to the sentence about lift.
C treats the diagram as decoration with no informational role, which is wrong.
D states something neither source claims.
solution.answer: A) It shows that lift is an upward arrow on the wings, matching the text's idea of an upward push

items.prompt:
Passage: After a new bridge opened in 2015, the village of Greenport became easier to reach. Shop owners reported more customers from neighboring towns. The passage says business picked up sharply in the years right after the bridge opened, though it does not give exact figures.

Table 1: Yearly sales at Greenport shops (in thousands of dollars)
2013: 80
2014: 82
2015: 95
2016: 130
2017: 138

Using both the passage and the table, which statement best describes what happened to sales after the bridge opened?
A) Sales stayed about the same every year
B) Sales jumped from 95 in 2015 to 130 in 2016, matching the text's claim that business picked up sharply
C) Sales were 80 in 2013, which proves the bridge helped
D) Sales reached 138, so the bridge made business better than any other cause
items.answer: B) Sales jumped from 95 in 2015 to 130 in 2016, matching the text's claim that business picked up sharply

steps: The text says business picked up sharply after the bridge opened in 2015 but gives no numbers, so the table fills that gap.
Sales went from 95 in 2015 to 130 in 2016, a large jump that matches 'picked up sharply.' Choice B combines both sources correctly.
A ignores the table, which shows a clear rise, not steady numbers.
C uses a year before the bridge opened, so it cannot show the bridge's effect.
D pulls the highest number but claims the bridge alone caused it, going beyond what either source supports.
solution.answer: B) Sales jumped from 95 in 2015 to 130 in 2016, matching the text's claim that business picked up sharply

items.prompt:
Passage: The article describes how a mountain glacier called Long Ice has been shrinking for decades. Warmer summers melt more ice than winter snow can replace. The passage says the glacier has lost much of its length but never states the exact amount.

Chart 1: Length of Long Ice glacier (in kilometers)
1990: 12
2000: 10
2010: 8
2020: 5

Using the chart to fill the detail the words leave out, by how much did Long Ice shrink from 1990 to 2020?
A) It shrank by 7 kilometers, from 12 down to 5
B) It shrank by 5 kilometers, because 5 is its length in 2020
C) It grew, because the numbers in the chart are large
D) The chart cannot tell us anything the words did not already say
items.answer: A) It shrank by 7 kilometers, from 12 down to 5

steps: The text says the glacier shrank but gives no amount, so the chart supplies the missing number.
From 1990 to 2020 the length went from 12 km to 5 km, a loss of 12 minus 5, which is 7 km. Choice A is correct.
B copies the 2020 length straight from the chart instead of finding the change, so it picks the wrong figure.
C contradicts both sources, since the numbers fall and the text says the glacier shrank.
D is wrong because the chart adds the exact amount the words left out.
solution.answer: A) It shrank by 7 kilometers, from 12 down to 5

items.prompt:
Passage: A nature article explains that honeybees tell each other where to find flowers by doing a special 'waggle dance' inside the hive. The direction a bee waggles points the other bees toward the food. The passage says the dance angle compared to straight up matches the direction of the flowers compared to the sun, but in words this is hard to picture.

Diagram 1: A honeybee's waggle dance
A bee waggles at a 45 degree angle to the right of straight up.
A note reads: 'Straight up means fly toward the sun.'
A note reads: '45 degrees right of up means fly 45 degrees to the right of the sun.'

How does the diagram clarify the confusing sentence about the dance angle?
A) It shows the hive is dark inside
B) It shows a real angle and explains that the dance angle equals the flower's angle from the sun, making the text's idea clear
C) It tells the reader that bees like flowers
D) It proves the bees are flying toward the sun itself
items.answer: B) It shows a real angle and explains that the dance angle equals the flower's angle from the sun, making the text's idea clear

steps: The text states a hard to picture idea: the dance angle matches the flower's direction relative to the sun.
The diagram gives a concrete example, a 45 degree waggle meaning fly 45 degrees right of the sun, which makes the abstract sentence clear. Choice B integrates both.
A and C report side facts that do not explain the angle relationship.
D misreads the diagram, since the bee points 45 degrees from the sun, not at the sun, and the bees fly to flowers, not the sun.
solution.answer: B) It shows a real angle and explains that the dance angle equals the flower's angle from the sun, making the text's idea clear

items.prompt:
Passage: A sports column argues that local minor league baseball is fading. The writer claims that fewer and fewer people come to the games each year and that the sport is 'losing fans every season.' The column urges the city to spend its money on other entertainment instead. It treats the decline as steady and certain. The writer never shows attendance numbers in the column itself.

Graph 1: Attendance at local minor league games (in thousands)
2019: 40
2020: 35
2021: 38
2022: 33
2023: 41

Using both the column and the graph, which statement best describes how the graph complicates the writer's claim?
A) The graph confirms the claim, because attendance is lower in 2020 than in 2019
B) The graph shows attendance actually rose in two seasons, 2021 and 2023, so the decline is not as steady as the writer says
C) The graph proves the writer is completely correct that fans leave every season
D) The graph just repeats the column and adds nothing new
items.answer: B) The graph shows attendance actually rose in two seasons, 2021 and 2023, so the decline is not as steady as the writer says

steps: The writer claims a steady, every season decline but shows no numbers, so the graph is needed to test the claim.

Attendance rose from 35 in 2020 to 38 in 2021, and from 33 in 2022 to 41 in 2023, so it went up in two seasons. That contradicts 'losing fans every season,' which complicates the claim. Choice B is correct.
A forces a match by noticing one drop while ignoring the rises, the misconception that the visual must agree with the text.
C ignores the data entirely and accepts the words alone.
D treats the graph as a mere repeat, missing that it adds numbers the column never gave.
solution.answer: B) The graph shows attendance actually rose in two seasons, 2021 and 2023, so the decline is not as steady as the writer says

items.prompt:
Passage: An article describes the journey of the explorer ship Dawnrunner along a river. The ship left Port Ash and first reached a tall waterfall, where the crew rested. Later they passed a stone tower built on a cliff. Near the end of the trip they anchored at a wide green delta before reaching the sea. The passage names these landmarks but does not say how far apart they are or give the crew's exact route.

Map 1: The Dawnrunner's river (listed from the river's start to its mouth at the sea)
Mile 0: Port Ash
Mile 15: Tall Waterfall
Mile 28: Stone Tower
Mile 40: Green Delta
Mile 45: Open Sea

Using both the passage and the map, which statement correctly orders the journey and adds a detail only the map supplies?
A) The crew rested at the Tall Waterfall at Mile 15, then passed the Stone Tower at Mile 28, then anchored at the Green Delta at Mile 40, all before reaching the sea
B) The crew reached the Green Delta first because it has the highest mile number
C) The crew passed the Stone Tower before the Tall Waterfall, because the tower sounds more important
D) The map only repeats the names in the passage and adds no new detail
items.answer: A) The crew rested at the Tall Waterfall at Mile 15, then passed the Stone Tower at Mile 28, then anchored at the Green Delta at Mile 40, all before reaching the sea

steps: The passage gives the order of landmarks but no distances, so the map adds the mile markers.

Reading the map from start to sea, the order is Waterfall (15), Tower (28), Delta (40), then Open Sea (45), which matches the passage and adds the distances. Choice A is correct and integrates both sources.
B confuses a higher mile number with happening first, getting the order backward.
C reorders the landmarks based on a guess instead of the map's mile markers.
D is wrong because the map supplies new distance details the words never gave.
solution.answer: A) The crew rested at the Tall Waterfall at Mile 15, then passed the Stone Tower at Mile 28, then anchored at the Green Delta at Mile 40, all before reaching the sea
